name: Ju'ane "Smurf" Kennell
headline: Education changes minds. Mentorship changes lives.
summary: Ju'ane Kennell entered prison at 19 and has spent more than two decades building a record of education, leadership, mentorship, faith, and service.
cardParagraphs: Ju'ane Kennell entered prison at 19 and has spent more than two decades building a record of education, leadership, mentorship, faith, and service.
His campaign materials emphasize continued growth, learning, and preparation for purpose beyond a life without parole sentence.
paragraphs: Ju'ane Kennell entered prison at 19 and was sentenced to life without parole. His campaign materials say he maintains his innocence and continues to fight for justice.

Inside prison, his materials describe a focus on education at Lincoln University, a Bachelor of Science path in Business Administration, certification in Braille, and service as a Puppies for Parole dog handler.
His story also centers mentoring, leadership, faith, education, and the belief that people sentenced as emerging adults should have a meaningful opportunity for review.
story: Ju'ane Kennell entered prison at 19 and has spent more than two decades building a record of education, leadership, mentorship, faith, and service.
quote: My story is why second chances matter.
accomplishments: Earned a GED and continued education through Lincoln University
Pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration
Certified in Braille
Certified Puppies for Parole dog handler
Served through mentoring, education, leadership, faith, and IPM programming
reviewReason: He was sentenced as an emerging adult and the campaign materials describe more than two decades of growth, learning, mentoring, and service.

name: Kenneth Gilbert
headline: Accountability, growth, service, and a better tomorrow.
summary: Kenneth Gilbert was 18 when he committed a crime. His story focuses on recovery, sobriety, education, accountability, service, and helping others make better choices.
cardParagraphs: Kenneth Gilbert was 18 when he committed a crime after what he describes as a year-long tailspin.
His story focuses on recovery, sobriety, education, accountability, service, and helping others make better choices.
paragraphs: Kenneth Gilbert describes being an honors student from the suburbs before a year-long tailspin that led to prison at 18.
Four years into his life without parole sentence, he volunteered for ITC and began what he describes as a lifelong journey of recovery, sobriety, education, and service.
His materials describe teaching classes, working with crime victims, sharing his story, and participating in leadership programs as part of a commitment to accountability and change.

name: Kenneth Bell
headline: A time to speak.
summary: Kenneth Bell was sentenced to life without parole at 19 and has built a record of education, leadership, writing, advocacy, and service while incarcerated.
cardParagraphs: Kenneth Bell was sentenced to life without parole at 19.
His campaign materials describe decades of education, leadership, writing, advocacy, and service inside prison.
paragraphs: Kenneth Bell's story poster says he was sentenced to life without parole in 1990 at the age of 19.
His materials list high school completion at Potosi Correctional Center, leadership as NAACP president at three prison branches, and admission to St. Louis University under a sentence of LWOP.
The poster also describes published writing, unpublished books, and artwork displayed at the St. Louis University Art Museum.

name: James "JD" Dunn
headline: Peace, leadership, ministry, and mentoring.
summary: James "JD" Dunn has been incarcerated for more than 30 years and describes spending his time peacefully while completing programs, serving in ministry leadership, mentoring through GLA, and working in the institutional parole office.
cardParagraphs: James "JD" Dunn has been incarcerated for more than 30 years.

paragraphs: James "JD" Dunn's story poster says he has been incarcerated for more than 30 years and has tried to spend that time as peacefully as possible.
His materials describe completing virtually every program offered at Jefferson City Correctional Center.

The poster also lists service on the Willow Creek Community Church leadership team, service with Rise Up Prison Ministry, original membership and coordination work with the Growth and Leadership Academy, employment in the institutional parole office, and GLA mentoring.
